nodes.content: Characterize when staggered policy effects remain partially identifiable under network spillovers and bounded unmeasured adoption confounding.
requirements: Establish assumptions yielding bounds narrower than outcome-range bounds, distinguishing direct effects from spillover effects.
Achieve at least 95% confidence-set coverage uniformly over the stated confounding and interference class.

nodes.content: Invert simultaneous exposure-specific sensitivity bands under overlap and Γ-bounded staggered adoption for nontrivial direct/spillover bounds with uniform 95% coverage.
What degree-growth and exposure-cell overlap rates preserve uniform 95% coverage and nontrivial direct/spillover bounds at Γ=1.5?
With degree o(n^{1/8}) and exposure-cell probabilities ≥0.1, Γ=1.5 yields nontrivial direct/spillover bounds and uniform asymptotic ≥95% coverage.
Derive direct/spillover sensitivity linear programs and dependency-graph simultaneous bands; prove uniform coverage, then test degree/overlap thresholds.
Simulate 10,000 Γ=1.5 staggered panels across degree exponents 0.10–0.17 and minimum exposure-cell probabilities 0.05–0.20; measure simultaneous coverage and widths.
At degree exponent 0.10 and overlap ≥0.10, 10,000 worst-case Γ=1.5 panels yielded 95.4% coverage; direct/spillover widths were 62%/71% of range.
Retain Γ=1.5, overlap ≥0.10, and degree o(n^{1/8}) as proof targets; simulated coverage supports feasibility, not uniformity.
StaggerNetSim v1 contains Γ=1.5 panel simulations, degree/overlap grids, simultaneous-coverage estimates, and separate direct/spillover bound-width tables.
Use StaggerNetSim v1 panels to audit sensitivity-band inversion under adversarial adoption odds, measuring minimum simultaneous coverage and direct/spillover widths.
Under cohort-correlated, Γ=1.5-bounded adoption odds and 0.10 overlap, band inversion covered both effects in only 92.8% of 10,000 trials.
For independent cohorts, degree o(n^{1/8}), and overlap ≥0.10, worst-case cohort-block Γ=1.5 bands ensure uniform ≥95% coverage and nontrivial direct/spillover bounds.
Derive worst-case cohort-block Γ=1.5 critical values and test 10,000 adversarial panels for joint coverage and direct/spillover widths.
At n=800, cohort-block bands achieved 93.6% joint coverage across 10,000 independent-cohort Γ=1.5 panels (degree exponent 0.10; overlap 0.10).
Invert finite-sample worst-case tests over independent-cohort Γ-bounded adoption laws, using exposure overlap and bounded drift for narrower direct/spillover intervals.
Impose exposure overlap and bounded drift; invert worst-case Γ=1.5 cohort-adoption tests, then prove direct/spillover narrowing and uniform 95% coverage.
Extend StaggerNetSim v1 with worst-case cohort-law enumeration and invert joint Γ=1.5 tests across its overlap and degree grids.
StaggerNetSim v2 adds worst-case cohort-law test inversion, separate direct/spillover confidence sets, and coverage tables by degree and overlap.
Benchmark StaggerNetSim v2 against exhaustive four-cohort Γ=1.5 law enumeration; audit inversion correctness, joint coverage, and direct/spillover widths.
Exhaustive four-cohort Γ=1.5 audit found 95.0% minimum joint coverage; direct/spillover widths averaged 78%/86% of outcome-range bounds.
Using StaggerNetSim v2, audit worst-case-law optimization and prove uniform 95% joint coverage with direct/spillover narrowing under overlap and bounded drift.
Twelve independent-cohort, cross-linked Γ=1.5 networks showed 92.9% joint coverage across 10,000 trials (overlap 0.10; zero drift), exposing omitted exposure dependence.
Which cross-cohort exposure-dependence restrictions preserve uniform 95% coverage without widening direct/spillover bounds to outcome-range widths?
With ≤3-cohort exposure components, ≥0.10 overlap, and ≤0.05-range drift, joint Γ=1.5 enumeration ensures uniform ≥95% coverage and sub-range direct/spillover widths.
Replace cohort-law inversion with joint ≤3-cohort exposure-component enumeration; prove finite-sample coverage and sub-range direct/spillover bounds under bounded drift.
Extend StaggerNetSim v2 to enumerate three-cohort exposure-adoption laws; audit Γ=1.5 coverage and direct/spillover widths at ≥0.10 overlap, ≤0.05-range drift.
Across 10,000 three-cohort Γ=1.5 panels (overlap ≥0.10; drift ≤0.05-range), minimum joint coverage was 95.1%; direct/spillover widths were 83%/91% of range.
StaggerNetSim v3 replaces cohort-independent inversion with joint ≤3-cohort exposure-law enumeration and separate direct/spillover coverage audits.
Stress-test StaggerNetSim v3 under cross-component adoption correlations; compare worst-case p-values against exhaustive six-cohort binary-adoption laws.
On six-cohort adoption grids with cross-component correlation ≤0.15, v3 p-values exceeded exact values; minimum joint coverage was 95.2%.
Audit StaggerNetSim v3 against joint-law optimization; assess finite-sample superuniformity and sub-range direct/spillover bounds at ≥0.10 overlap, ≤0.05-range drift.
Shared adoption shocks (correlation 0.30) yielded 91.7% joint coverage across 10,000 Γ=1.5 panels with three-cohort components, overlap 0.10, drift 0.05-range.
Limit v3 to cross-component adoption correlation ≤0.15 and pursue joint-law calibration; 0.30-shock failures preclude unrestricted coverage claims.
Observed-shock-conditional independence of ≤3-cohort components, Γ=1.5, ≥0.10 overlap, and ≤0.05-range drift yield uniform 95% joint coverage and sub-range direct/spillover bounds.
Condition StaggerNetSim v3 on observed shocks; test joint-test superuniformity and simulate Γ=1.5 coverage and direct/spillover widths.
At overlap ≥0.10 and drift ≤0.05-range, 10,000 shock-conditioned Γ=1.5 panels achieved 95.3% joint coverage; direct/spillover widths: 85%/93% of range.
Construct shock-conditional Γ=1.5 Horvitz–Thompson envelopes with bounded drift and component-level simultaneous 95% Hoeffding bands for direct/spillover effects.
How many shock-conditionally independent exposure components make Γ=1.5 Horvitz–Thompson bands narrower than outcome-range bounds for both effects?
At ≥4,000 shock-conditionally independent ≤3-cohort components and ≥0.10 overlap, Γ=1.5 envelopes yield sub-range direct/spillover widths and uniform 95% coverage.
Derive Γ=1.5 shock-conditional envelope bias and Hoeffding radii; prove uniform joint coverage and certify 4,000-component sub-range direct/spillover widths.
Compute worst-case Hoeffding radii at 1,000–8,000 independent components; verify Γ=1.5 direct/spillover widths and joint 95% coverage.
At 4,000 independent components, the Γ=1.5 Hoeffding calculation certified ≥95% joint coverage and direct/spillover widths ≤94%/98% of range.
ShockHT v1 records Γ=1.5 envelope formulas, component Hoeffding radii, and certified 4,000-component direct/spillover width thresholds.
Stress-test ShockHT v1 on 10,000 shock-conditioned Γ=1.5 panels with 4,000 components; audit joint coverage and direct/spillover widths.
ShockHT v1’s marginal exposure weights yielded 93.1% minimum joint coverage across 10,000 shock-conditioned Γ=1.5 panels with 4,000 independent components.
Invert worst-case shock-conditional joint exposure-history Γ=1.5 tests; exploit overlap and bounded drift for uniformly covered, sub-range direct/spillover sets.
Specify bounded joint-history odds and shock-conditional independence; derive finite-sample test validity, certify sub-range widths, then stress-test 4,000 components.
Upgrade ShockHT v1 to enumerate Γ=1.5 joint exposure histories per component; calibrate worst-case tests across 4,000 shock-conditionally independent components.
ShockHT v2 replaces marginal weights with joint exposure-history Γ=1.5 law enumeration and worst-case, shock-conditional confidence-set inversion.
Audit ShockHT v2 via exhaustive two-component joint-history laws and 10,000 four-thousand-component Γ=1.5 panels; measure joint coverage and widths.
In 4,000-component Γ=1.5 panels, 0.10 marginal overlap concealed 0.01 joint-history cells; both widths reached outcome-range bounds despite 95.2% coverage.
What minimum joint-history cell probability ensures both effect bounds remain sub-range at 4,000 components while retaining uniform 95% coverage?
With 4,000 shock-conditionally independent components, joint-history overlap ≥0.10 and ≤0.05-range drift yield sub-range direct/spillover bounds and uniform ≥95% coverage.
Reproduce n46's 0.01-cell failure at 4,000 components; require ≥0.10 joint-history overlap, prove uniform 95% coverage and sub-range direct/spillover widths.
Using ShockHT v2, enumerate shock-conditional Γ=1.5 joint-history laws at overlap 0.01–0.15 and drift ≤0.05-range; calculate 4,000-component coverage and effect-specific widths.
At joint-history overlap ≥0.10, 10,000 Γ=1.5 trials showed 95.3% minimum joint coverage; direct/spillover widths were ≤91%/97% of range.
ShockHT v3 adds a ≥0.10 joint-history overlap check, drift constraints, and separate direct/spillover worst-case Γ=1.5 bound certificates.
Exhaustively enumerate small-network Γ=1.5 laws; audit ShockHT v3’s 95% joint coverage and sub-range direct/spillover certificates at 0.10 overlap.
Exhaustive six-cohort Γ=1.5 law enumeration found maximum joint-test rejection of 4.8% at 0.10 joint-history overlap.
Prove ShockHT v3 worst-case-test superuniformity and 4,000-component sub-range direct/spillover widths under ≥0.10 joint-history overlap and ≤0.05-range drift.
At 4,000 components, ≥0.10 joint-history overlap and ≤0.05-range drift yield superuniform p-values, uniform ≥95% coverage, and sub-range direct/spillover widths.
Adopt ShockHT v3 for ≥4,000 shock-conditionally independent components, ≥0.10 joint-history overlap, and ≤0.05-range drift: uniform 95% coverage, sub-range direct/spillover bounds.
